original.target_description: Experiment 1: effect of seven levels of facial redness on perceived anger ratings across angry and neutral computer-generated Caucasian male faces, in the Baruch College participant sample; within-subject redness effect for anger ratings, F(6, 234) = 4.91.

n.sample_role: Participants in Experiment 1 repeated-measures anger-rating analysis; recruited sample retained in the reported test, consistent with the reported repeated-measures degrees of freedom.
n.exclusions: No exclusions reported in Experiment 1 methods/results; forty recruited participants and the reported degrees of freedom support the full sample for this test.
n.location: Article p. 52 (PDF page 4), Experiment 1, Method, Participants; Results, anger-rating redness effect.

es.metric: partial eta squared (η²p; canonical text renders h2p)
es.location: Article p. 52 (PDF page 4), Experiment 1, Results, right column, effect of red on anger ratings.

p.location: Article p. 52 (PDF page 4), Experiment 1, Results, right column, same anger-rating redness effect F(6, 234) = 4.91.

replication.target_description: Wolf et al., Study 2, p. 25 reports two distinct default-versus-red anger comparisons: presence-of-demand within-subjects sample and absence-of-demand between-subjects sample. The supplied study/outcome/page and requested d do not identify which comparison is assigned. Both audit_ids 784 and 785 have identical locators; input order was not used to assign tests.

n.sample_role: Unresolved between 111 participants measured twice in the presence-of-demand condition and 104 default-only plus 114 red-only participants in the absence-of-demand conditions; no generic total used as target analytic n.
n.exclusions: Target subgroup unresolved; Study 2 reports 489 recruited and 160 exclusions, leaving 329 overall.

reported_success.location: p. 25, Test for the Design-Dependency of the Red-Anger Effect
reported_success.quote:
As hypothesized, we replicated the red-anger effect
in the within-subjects design whereas it vanished in the between-subjects design.

notes:
Original acquisition: DOI landing inaccessible; publisher PDF returned 403 (not retried); Unpaywall and OpenAlex reported no open full-text location; exact-title open-web searches found no accessible primary full text. Replication title verified against input and first page; acquired OSF primary file EMO_demandcharacteristics_v1.pdf via public API. Study 2 narrative verdict is study-level mixed, not a verdict assigned to either unresolved contrast. No test or effect assigned using audit_id/input ordering. Candidate tests on p. 25: unpaired presence-of-demand comparison t(220), and absence-of-demand comparison t(216); paired sensitivity test is also printed. A condition identifier is required to select the target.
Source follow-up: Original-only fresh extraction. Published Cognition and Emotion article, volume 32(1), pp. 49–60 (issue 2018; copyright 2016), matching title/authors/DOI in the assigned reference. Visually inspected rendered PDF page 4 (article p. 52) of the named EBSCO PDF. The printed anger-rating partial eta squared is .11; the frozen canonical text drops the decimal and renders it as h2p = 11. The es.value preserves the visually confirmed printed .11; the quotation preserves the canonical text verbatim. This is the omnibus redness effect specifically on anger ratings, not the combined anger/health main effect, interaction, quadratic trend or sex subgroup tests. All three assigned rows have identical original-side study, neutral description and page locator, so the same test is independently applicable. Requested metric is eta squared; the source specifically prints partial eta squared, retained without conversion. Unassigned replication and reported_success are null placeholders; no replication source examined.
